result.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService deleteEvent, the diff changes `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.externalId;` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is falsy, the find condition can never match, so calendarId becomes undefined instead of the old fallback to the destination calendar's externalId, and calendar.events.delete is then called with an undefined calendarId — the orphaned-event behavior described is a direct consequence of this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` change the fallback calendar selection from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. If `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, the `.find(...)` predicate can never match any real `cal.externalId`, so this resolves to `undefined` instead of using the event’s destination calendar (old behavior). This can break cancellation/update for bookings whose reference lacks `externalCalendarId` by targeting the wrong calendar (or potentially passing an undefined calendarId depending on how it’s used below).
